step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard architecture depicts 'CrazyWall', a fraud detection system at Careem divided into 'Historical' (top) and 'Real Time' (bottom) processing layers. Historical ETL reads from S3, processed by EMR, loading user identity graph data into Neptune. Real-time events enter via SQS into Elastic Beanstalk (core codebase), which writes/reads to Neptune for user graph lookup. Classification results are written to RDS, while suspicious/high-value customer alerts flow through an API (API Blocking) to a Ticketing System. Graph query access is exposed via API (API Crazywall) to Users and a UI. Neptune ML is shown as a future ML integration block.
